papers.title: Kubrick: Multimodal Agent Collaborations for Synthetic Video Generation
papers.venue: CVPR AI for Content Creation Workshop
papers.findings: 多智能体可通过 Blender 程序与视觉反馈生成受控合成视频。
papers.limitations: 依赖资产、函数库与 Blender 知识；公开代码未确认。

papers.title: From Data to Story: Towards Automatic Animated Data Video Creation with LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
papers.findings: LLM agents can orchestrate executable visualization specifications, narration and video composition.
papers.limitations: Small empirical scope and no confirmed public code.

papers.title: LogoMotion: Visually-Grounded Code Synthesis for Creating and Editing Animation
papers.findings: Visually grounded repair and code-connected controls improve content-aware animation authoring.
papers.limitations: Limited to layered logos and dependent on input layer quality.

papers.title: TheoremExplainAgent: Towards Video-based Multimodal Explanations for LLM Theorem Understanding
papers.findings: Hierarchical planning extends Manim explanations to multi-minute videos.
papers.limitations: Long videos accumulate overlap, sizing and alignment errors.

papers.title: MG-Gen: Single Image to Motion Graphics Generation
papers.findings: Layered code animation preserves text and geometry better than pixel-space I2V baselines.
papers.limitations: Layer decomposition errors propagate and the domain is planar design.

papers.title: Manimator: Transforming Research Papers into Visual Explanations
papers.findings: A simple planning-to-code pipeline provides a strong Manim baseline.
papers.limitations: No video-feedback loop and strong dependence on the base model.

papers.title: Code2Video: A Code-centric Paradigm for Educational Video Generation
papers.findings: Code-centric generation with scoped repair and visual criticism improves educational video generation.
papers.limitations: Manim and education specific; VLM and TeachQuiz validity require external replication.

papers.title: LLM2Manim: Pedagogy-Aware AI Generation of STEM Animations
papers.findings: Pedagogical constraints and expert gating can improve measured learning outcomes.
papers.limitations: Semi-automatic, limited topics and student sample, and requires expert review.

papers.title: PhysicsSolutionAgent: Towards Multimodal Explanations for Numerical Physics Problem Solving
papers.findings: Execution and screenshot feedback support multi-minute physics explanations.
papers.limitations: Small sample and VLM feedback can be misleading.

papers.title: Beyond End-to-End Video Models: An LLM-Based Multi-Agent System for Educational Video Generation
papers.findings: Constrained scripts and deterministic assembly can support industrial-scale production.
papers.limitations: Relies on templates and proprietary infrastructure; deployment claims are hard to reproduce.

papers.title: DATAREEL: Automated Data-Driven Video Story Generation with Animations
papers.findings: Multi-agent generation improves over direct prompting but timeline coordination remains difficult.
papers.limitations: Derived annotations may be noisy and evaluation relies on VLMs.

papers.title: Training and Agentic Inference Strategies for LLM-based Manim Animation Generation
papers.findings: Training and renderer-in-the-loop inference improve complementary aspects of code animation generation.
papers.limitations: Reference similarity is not teaching quality and the benchmark scope is narrow.

papers.title: ANVIL: Analogies and Videos for Lecturers
papers.findings: Intermediate screenplays and teacher review support usable analogy animations.
papers.limitations: Proxy metrics do not establish pedagogical correctness and the study is small.

papers.title: ALGOGEN: Tool-Generated Verifiable Traces for Reliable Algorithm Visualization
papers.findings: Separating verified execution traces from rendering reduces hallucination and layout instability.
papers.limitations: Template renderers limit visual freedom and success does not establish learning effectiveness.

papers.title: ManimAgent: Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents for Visual Education
papers.findings: Curated success and failure memory can improve first-pass performance on a fixed probe.
papers.limitations: Memory contamination risk and evaluation focuses on short single-scene animation.

papers.title: LottieGPT: Tokenizing Vector Animation for Autoregressive Generation
papers.findings: Models can generate compact, editable, resolution-independent temporal programs.
papers.limitations: Lottie has limited expressiveness and long complex animations remain difficult.

papers.title: InternSVG: Towards Unified SVG Tasks with Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.findings: Unified SVG multitask training supports dynamic SVG generation alongside static tasks.
papers.limitations: Dynamic video is only one part of the work and long-form complexity is limited.

papers.title: Training and Benchmarking Code Generation for Physics-Inspired Animations
papers.findings: Executable and dynamically correct physics animation remains difficult even when code runs.
papers.limitations: Qualitative rather than precise simulation; synthetic data and VLM reward are imperfect.

papers.title: Reels-RSI: Program-Level Self-Improvement for Code-Rendered Explainer Videos
papers.findings: Executable rules enable auditing and can reduce violations, especially for weaker agents.
papers.limitations: Single system and model family; small field study and judge position bias.

papers.title: MoVer: Motion Verification for Motion Graphics Animations
papers.findings: Explicit spatiotemporal predicates provide localized feedback and improve constraint satisfaction.
papers.limitations: The DSL covers predefined relations and many repair rounds are costly.

papers.title: SGA: Plug & Play Geometric Verification for Educational Video Synthesis
papers.findings: Symbolic geometry checks can outperform a VLM critic for layout conflicts.
papers.limitations: Only geometry is checked; AABB approximations miss some conflicts.

papers.title: ManiBench: A Benchmark for Testing Visual-Logic Drift and Syntactic Hallucinations in Manim Code Generation
papers.findings: Model scale alone does not guarantee Manim proficiency.
papers.limitations: Only 12 pilot tasks; heuristic alignment and coverage do not establish visual correctness.

papers.title: Code2Video-Compass: A Comprehensive Benchmark for General-Purpose Code-Based Video Generation across T2V, I2V, and V2V
papers.findings: Execution reliability and video quality diverge, and performance falls with program complexity.
papers.limitations: Reliance on proprietary models and MLLM judges; reproducibility requires continued verification.

papers.title: Animation2Code: Evaluating Temporal Visual Reasoning in Video-to-Code Generation
papers.findings: High execution and appearance scores can coexist with poor temporal reconstruction.
papers.limitations: Short web animations and inherent program non-uniqueness.

papers.title: PhySimCode: A Benchmark and Evaluation Method for Physics Video to Code Generation
papers.findings: Models can state physics laws but struggle to infer them and recover parameters from video.
papers.limitations: Programmatic-to-real gap and many equivalent simulations.

papers.title: 4DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agents on Inverse Graphics of Dynamic Scenes
papers.findings: Static appearance and geometry ability do not transfer reliably to complex dynamics.
papers.limitations: High execution budget and difficult equivalence judgments among free-form programs.

papers.title: VideoCoCo: Code-as-CoT for Physically-Consistent Video Generation via an Agentic Dual-Engine System
papers.findings: Executable simulation drafts can improve physical consistency in a downstream generative editor.
papers.limitations: The final video is not deterministic code rendering and may reintroduce hallucination.

papers.title: VAnim: Rendering-Aware Sparse State Modeling for Structure-Preserving Vector Animation
papers.findings: Persistent objects plus sparse updates reduce sequence length and identity drift.
papers.limitations: SVG only; no audio or multi-shot narrative, and learned rewards miss maintainability.

papers.title: Keyframer: Empowering Animation Design using Large Language Models
papers.findings: Animation authoring benefits from decomposition, persistent context and parameter-level control.
papers.limitations: Requires existing SVG and covers a restricted set of CSS motion.

papers.title: Render-in-the-Loop: Vector Graphics Generation via Visual Self-Feedback
papers.findings: Effective visual self-feedback requires trajectories that teach the model canvas-to-next-code mapping.
papers.limitations: Static SVG and repeated rendering cost.

papers.title: CANVAS: Consistency-Aware Navigation via Visual Adaptive Sampling for Long-Context Text-to-SVG Generation
papers.findings: Budgeted future rollouts can improve long visual programs without retraining.
papers.limitations: Static output and high rollout cost.

papers.title: Hierarchical SVG Tokenization: Learning Compact Visual Programs for Scalable Vector Graphics Modeling
papers.status: preprint; author list incomplete in source brief
papers.findings: Geometry-aware hierarchical tokens shorten long visual programs.
papers.limitations: Static SVG and specialized vocabulary may reduce edit transparency.

papers.title: VectorGym: A Multi-Task Benchmark for SVG Code Generation, Sketching and Editing
papers.status: preprint; author list incomplete in source brief
papers.findings: Joint generation, understanding and editing offers a useful template for editable visual programs.
papers.limitations: No time dimension and judges may ignore code structure.

papers.title: StarVector: Generating Scalable Vector Graphics Code from Images and Text
papers.status: preprint; author list incomplete in source brief
papers.findings: Visual inputs can be mapped to semantic executable vector code.
papers.limitations: Static output and no temporal identity model.

papers.title: OmniSVG: A Unified Scalable Vector Graphics Generation Model
papers.status: published; author list incomplete in source brief
papers.findings: Unified SVG generation scales from icons to complex characters.
papers.limitations: Static output and no guarantee of animation-ready groups or topology.

papers.title: DeTikZify: Synthesizing Graphics Programs for Scientific Figures and Sketches with TikZ
papers.findings: Compilation and rendering provide reliable feedback for structured scientific graphics.
papers.limitations: Static scientific figures and costly TeX compilation.

papers.title: Design2Code: Benchmarking Multimodal Code Generation for Automated Front-End Engineering
papers.findings: Real webpages expose layout and long-code failures relevant to static scene reconstruction.
papers.limitations: No animation timeline or video-level temporal evaluation.

papers.title: Spellburst: A Node-based Interface for Exploratory Creative Coding with Natural Language Prompts
papers.findings: Branching, merging and parameter controls preserve exploratory creative workflows.
papers.limitations: HCI prototype without dedicated temporal consistency evaluation.

papers.title: DeepSVG: A Hierarchical Generative Network for Vector Graphics Animation
papers.findings: Path-level hierarchy and fixed-topology interpolation support smooth vector morphing.
papers.limitations: Animation is latent interpolation rather than language-to-animation code.

papers.title: Breathing Life Into Sketches Using Text-to-Video Priors
papers.status: preprint; author list incomplete in source brief
papers.findings: Video priors can optimize editable vector motion without a dedicated animation dataset.
papers.limitations: Slow optimization and unstable stroke topology.

papers.title: LiveSVG: Zero-Shot SVG Animation via Video Generation
papers.findings: Generated video can act as a motion proposal that is distilled into editable vector states.
papers.limitations: Not direct code synthesis; expensive fitting and difficult topology changes.

papers.title: SceneCraft: An LLM Agent for Synthesizing 3D Scene as Blender Code
papers.status: published; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Scene graphs and solvers handle layout while VLMs diagnose semantic mismatch.
papers.limitations: Static-scene focus, asset dependence and incomplete animation coverage.

papers.title: 3D-GPT: Procedural 3D Modeling with Large Language Models
papers.status: preprint; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Executable DCC code provides editable procedural parameters rather than a terminal mesh.
papers.limitations: Function-library bounded, weak quantitative benchmark and limited systematic repair.

papers.title: LL3M: Large Language 3D Modelers
papers.status: preprint; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Shared executable code acts as both representation and memory for local repair.
papers.limitations: Mostly object-level and original model service is retired.

papers.title: Agentic 3D Creation via Joint Agent–Program Design
papers.status: preprint; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Jointly designed relational DSLs shift numerical geometry from the LLM to the executor.
papers.limitations: Expressiveness is bounded by the DSL and component library.

papers.title: SceneCode: Executable World Programs for Editable Indoor Scenes with Articulated Objects
papers.status: preprint; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Programs can unify scene layout with simulator-loadable articulated assets.
papers.limitations: Indoor domain and weak art detail and physical parameters.

papers.title: Nova3D: Code-Native Generation of Programmable 3D Assets
papers.status: preprint; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Native addressable parts and joints are essential for production-ready generated assets.
papers.limitations: Small system-related benchmark and asset-level focus.

papers.title: BlenderLLM: Training LLMs for CAD with Self-improvement
papers.status: preprint; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Domain data and self-improvement can teach a medium code model Blender CAD scripting.
papers.limitations: Simple CAD objects, judge bias and Blender-version risk.

papers.title: GS-Agent: Creating 4D Physical Worlds with Generative Simulation
papers.status: preprint; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: A simulation engine turns physical motion into an executable and inspectable program.
papers.limitations: Sensitive to assets and physical parameters; code release not fully confirmed.

papers.title: GPT4Motion: Scripting Physical Motions in Text-to-Video Generation
papers.status: published; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Physics-code drafts can control a higher-fidelity pixel generator.
papers.limitations: Limited primitives and diffusion may break geometry and identity.

papers.title: AutoUE: Automated Generation of 3D Games in Unreal Engine via Multi-Agent Systems
papers.status: preprint; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: End-to-end games require compiling and testing runtime interaction, not only rendering scenes.
papers.limitations: Small task set and fragile engine, plugin and asset configuration.

papers.title: UnrealLLM
papers.status: published; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Mature PCG systems offer more scalable control than hard-coded per-object placement.
papers.limitations: Heavy UE dependencies and asset retrieval bounds quality.

papers.title: Authoring for Living Worlds: Tool-Constrained LLM Agents for Executable Multi-Actor Scenarios
papers.status: preprint; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: State constraints enforced at every operation can outperform post-hoc validation.
papers.limitations: Fixed game assets and action registry bound the world and visual quality.

papers.title: Cutscene Agent
papers.status: preprint; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Cutscene generation unifies scene, animation, camera and audio as temporal authoring.
papers.limitations: Tool legality does not ensure valid world state; full code release unconfirmed.

papers.title: 3DCodeBench
papers.status: preprint; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Joint 2D, 3D and execution metrics expose errors hidden by a hero render.
papers.limitations: Asset-heavy Infinigen distribution and subjective judge component.

papers.title: Code4Scene
papers.status: preprint; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Persistent scene-state checks catch intersection and unintended edits hidden by rendered images.
papers.limitations: UE-specific, modest size and dependent on engine/tool versions.

papers.title: Holodeck: Language Guided Generation of 3D Embodied AI Environments
papers.status: published; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Simulator compatibility and interaction properties matter more than photorealism for embodied scenes.
papers.limitations: Asset retrieval and layout focus; limited visual repair and no new topology.

papers.title: RoboGen
papers.status: published; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Generating executable worlds and supervision can scale robot skill data.
papers.limitations: Reward errors and simulation-to-real gap; implementation variants differ.

papers.title: FilmAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for End-to-End Film Automation in Virtual 3D Spaces
papers.status: published; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Role-specialized agents and persistent engine state support virtual film production.
papers.limitations: Mostly selects predefined stages, actions and shots rather than open code generation.

papers.title: Scene Co-pilot
papers.status: preprint; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Human-in-the-loop editing and reusable code assets are practical for controllable video production.
papers.limitations: Limited automatic evaluation and incomplete release status.

papers.title: BlenderAlchemy
papers.status: published; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Small reversible edits to node graphs are more stable than full scene rewrites.
papers.limitations: Focused on material, lighting and local editing rather than general scene generation.

papers.title: The Scene Language
papers.status: preprint; full author list unavailable in source brief
papers.findings: Separating structure, category semantics and appearance identity links programs with neural rendering.
papers.limitations: Weaker mapping to mature DCC and game-engine interaction semantics.

papers.title: TeachMaster: Generative Teaching via Code
papers.findings: Multi-agent planning → design → rendering pipeline that writes Manim scripts (Gemini-3 or a locally tuned Qwen3-32B) and aligns TTS narration by speaking rate; a quality-validation stage targets execution instability, timing misalignment and layout errors. Authors report course-video cost at roughly 0.3% of traditional production.
papers.limitations: Code not released as of cutoff; cost and quality figures are author-reported deployment numbers without an independent benchmark comparison.

papers.title: OmniLottie: Generating Vector Animations via Parameterized Lottie Tokens
papers.findings: A Lottie tokenizer turns shapes, animation functions and control parameters into compact command+parameter tokens on top of a pretrained VLM, enabling text/image/video-conditioned, interleaved multimodal generation of editable Lottie animations; releases MMLottie-2M and MMLottieBench. Authors report success rates of 97.3% / 92.0% / 90.7% for text-, text+image- and video-to-Lottie.
papers.limitations: Restricted to the Lottie feature subset covered by the tokenizer; under the authors' five-level failure taxonomy, residual errors are mainly structural (empty/malformed content) and rendering failures, and failure rates rise with input complexity.

papers.title: VibeVideoBench: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation
papers.findings: 239 bilingual tasks across 12 categories; agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, etc.) must deliver an MP4 with sound within one hour in a Docker sandbox. Over 2,151 rollouts from 9 agent systems, the best still misses a core requirement on about a quarter of tasks, and roughly three quarters of lost videos come from final renders started late, too slow, or never started.
papers.limitations: Very recent preprint; code listed as coming soon at cutoff. Judges agree on system rankings but only moderately on individual videos, so per-video scores should be read cautiously.

papers.title: Code Video Model: Conditioning Video Generation on Code
papers.findings: An LLM writes a Three.js program (scene, objects, camera, equation-driven dynamics) that renders a proxy video and reference image in under a minute; a pretrained video model is then steered with training-free early-step conditioning. Author-reported CodeVideoBench overall scores exceed a VACE baseline under three different judges.
papers.limitations: Final pixels come from a generative video model, so rendering is not deterministic and hallucination can re-enter; technical report with team authorship only, no peer review; benchmark and judges are author-defined.

papers.title: VisPhyWorld: Probing Physical Reasoning via Code-Driven Video Reconstruction
papers.findings: VisPhyBench (209 scenes from 108 templates) asks MLLMs to reconstruct a physical video as executable simulation code; 97.7% of reconstructions render validly, yet physics backends (Three.js/P5.js) are markedly more consistent than SVG/Manim, and models struggle to infer physical parameters.
papers.limitations: Synthetic rigid-body scenes only; Unreal/Blender backends were unreliable in the authors' attempts; render validity does not imply correct dynamics.

papers.title: Paper2Video: Automatic Video Generation from Scientific Papers
papers.findings: PaperTalker compiles LLM-written Beamer slides with tree-search layout refinement, then adds cursor grounding, subtitles, TTS and a talking head; the 101-paper benchmark introduces presentation-specific metrics such as PresentQuiz.
papers.limitations: Code generates static slides; temporal behaviour comes from TTS, cursor and talking-head composition rather than an executable animation program, hence adjacent rather than core.
